tweaks.signOut: Signing out may be required after applying or undoing this setting.
tweaks.notice: Status reflects stored settings, not guaranteed policy effects. Original values are backed up automatically for new tweaks; sign out manually when needed. On managed PCs, your organization may override settings.
tweak.err.originalMissing: No original backup for '{0}'. Select an earlier folder using Restore from backup; defaults will not be substituted.
tweaks.confirm.apply:
Do you really want to do this?

Apply the selected tweaks ({0})?

Registry values and system parameters will be backed up first. A backup error stops application. Legacy command tweaks use a declared undo, not an exact snapshot.
Creating a restore point is also recommended.
tweaks.confirm.undo:
Do you really want to do this?

Undo the selected tweaks ({0})?

Registry values and system parameters return to their state before the first application. Legacy commands use their declared undo. Later external changes to these settings will be replaced.
tweak.explorer-this-pc.name: Open This PC in File Explorer
tweak.explorer-this-pc.description: New File Explorer windows open This PC instead of Home or Quick access.
tweak.hide-recent-files.name: Hide recent files and frequent folders
tweak.hide-recent-files.description: Hides these lists from File Explorer Home and Quick access. Files and pinned folders are not deleted.
tweak.confirm-recycle-delete.name: Confirm moving files to the Recycle Bin
tweak.confirm-recycle-delete.description: File Explorer asks before moving a file to the Recycle Bin. This does not replace backups.
tweak.disable-autoplay.name: Disable AutoPlay for media
tweak.disable-autoplay.description: Windows will not automatically offer or launch actions when media is connected. Files can still be opened manually.
tweak.hide-taskbar-widgets.name: Hide Widgets and News and interests
tweak.hide-taskbar-widgets.description: Hides the Widgets button on Windows 11 or News and interests on Windows 10 22H2. Components are not uninstalled.
tweak.taskbar-align-left.name: Left-align the taskbar
tweak.taskbar-align-left.description: Moves Start and taskbar icons to the left. Windows 11 only.
tweak.disable-animations.name: Disable interface animations
tweak.disable-animations.description: Disables system window, menu, tooltip and list animations. Third-party apps may use their own effects.
tweak.disable-transparency.name: Disable transparency effects
tweak.disable-transparency.description: Makes Windows system surfaces opaque without changing the selected light or dark theme.
tweak.disable-accessibility-hotkeys.name: Disable StickyKeys and FilterKeys activation shortcuts
tweak.disable-accessibility-hotkeys.desc: Pressing Shift five times or holding right Shift no longer activates these features. Enabled accessibility features and their other settings are preserved.
tweak.disable-advertising-id.name: Disable the advertising ID
tweak.disable-advertising-id.description: Prevents apps from using this user's advertising ID for personalized ads. Does not block all advertising.
tweak.disable-delivery-peering.name: Disable update sharing with other PCs
tweak.disable-delivery-peering.descripti: Delivery Optimization uses HTTP without peer-to-peer transfers. Windows Update and Microsoft Store keep working. Supported on Pro, Enterprise and Education, not Home.
tweak.hide-lock-screen-notifications.des: Hides ordinary notifications and their contents until unlocked. Notifications in the unlocked session, calls and alarms remain enabled.
tweak.show-file-extensions.name: Show file extensions
tweak.show-file-extensions.description: Displays file extensions (.txt, .exe, etc.) in File Explorer. Automatically restarts File Explorer.
tweak.show-hidden-files.name: Show hidden files
tweak.show-hidden-files.description: Shows hidden files, but not protected operating system files. Automatically restarts File Explorer.
tweak.disable-start-recommendations.name: Disable Start recommendations and promotional tips
tweak.disable-start-recommendations.desc: Reduces suggested apps, tips and promotional notifications. Availability depends on the Windows version.
tweak.disable-explorer-ads.name: Disable File Explorer promotional notifications
tweak.disable-explorer-ads.description: Disables sync provider notifications such as OneDrive promotions in File Explorer.
tweak.disable-bing-search.name: Disable Bing suggestions in Start search
tweak.disable-bing-search.description: Configures search to use local results instead of Bing suggestions. Policy behavior depends on Windows edition and build.
tweak.disable-telemetry.name: Reduce diagnostic data and disable DiagTrack
tweak.disable-telemetry.description: Reduces Microsoft diagnostic data and disables Connected User Experiences and Telemetry. Undo sets the service to automatic; its original service state is not saved.
tweak.enable-long-paths.name: Enable long paths
tweak.enable-long-paths.description: Allows paths longer than 260 characters in applications that support long paths. Useful for development and deeply nested archives.
tweak.disable-hibernation.name: Disable hibernation
tweak.disable-hibernation.description: Removes hiberfil.sys to free disk space. Hibernation and Fast Startup stop working. Undo enables hibernation rather than restoring its original configuration.

bloat.title: Built-in apps
bloat.notice: Removal applies to the current user. Apps removed via WPIC can be restored from the built-in Windows image. The colored indicator shows how safe it is to remove an app; system apps marked as non-removable cannot be selected.
bloat.err.noneRestore: No removed apps selected for restore.
bloat.confirm.remove:
Do you really want to do this?

Remove the selected built-in apps ({0})?

Apps will be removed for the current user. Red indicators mean system risk — remove such apps only if you understand the consequences. Apps removed via WPIC can be restored with the Restore selected button.
Creating a restore point is also recommended.
bloat.confirm.restore:
Do you really want to do this?

Restore the selected apps ({0})?

Apps will be re-registered from the built-in Windows image. If the image does not contain the package, restore may fail.
